Context management

Read the right thing first.

The context advisor answers one question — what should be read for this task — and answers it with locators: a file and its line range, a session id, a cited repository path. Every turn starts with that answer, and every source says whether it could answer at all.

What arrives without being asked for#

Jeden already loads what is always true: the discovered context files (JEDEN.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, RULES.md, ~/.jeden/instructions.md, ~/.jeden/context.md) and the memories recorded for the working directory. Neither answers what is relevant to the request that just arrived.

The advisor answers that second question in the turn prologue. Before the first model call, the task text is matched against the configured sources and the result is appended to the turn as a [Context recommendations] block: one line per recommendation with its source, its exact locator, its heading and a snippet, followed by every source that answered nothing and why. The block is recorded in the session's own user event, so what the model received is auditable afterwards.

The block is bounded by context.advisor.maxChars and carries the sentence ranked matches, not verified answers: a recommendation is a place to look, never a fact. Set context.advisor.enabled to false to stop injecting it; jeden context prompt "&lt;task&gt;" prints exactly what a turn would receive, and says so when the advisor is off.

The four sources, and who owns each#

files reads everything readable under the declared roots — documentation, source code, configuration, manifests — and ranks it in chunks. Markdown is cut at its headings, because that is where its meaning starts; every other file is cut into forty-line windows titled by the window's first line at column zero, which in source is the declaration the rest of the window belongs to. The locator is path:first-last, so the answer can be read directly. Roots are declared in context.advisor.roots as colon-separated path or path@depth entries and default to the project plus ~/.jeden. A file with a zero byte in its head is not text and is skipped, a file over 256 KB is skipped, and .gitignore is respected.

memory recalls what earlier sessions wrote down for this working directory. The store and its ranking belong to Jeden's memory subsystem — ~/.jeden/memory.sqlite3, scope repo:&lt;cwd&gt; — and the locator is memory:&lt;id&gt;. An empty store is reported as an empty store, not as a missing match.

transcripts asks Transcript Lake, which owns the masked canonical archive of every recorded agent session. The advisor runs that product's own search command rather than reading its files, so the masking stays applied; the locator is session:&lt;id&gt;, which jeden show and the recall_conversation tool read.

ground-truth asks the Wisent ground-truth index, which owns cited answers across the organization's repositories. The locator is the citation it returns — repo/path@commit:first-last. The endpoint comes from context.advisor.groundTruthUrl, or from WISENT_GROUND_TRUTH_API or GROUND_TRUTH_API when that is empty; jeden context sources reports which of the three it used.

Every source answers, and each one is bounded#

context.advisor.sources defaults to all: nothing is left out of a search because it happened to be slow. The sources run concurrently, so a turn waits for the slowest one rather than for their sum, and each one is cut off by a deadline.

There are two deadlines because the two callers are different. context.advisor.promptTimeoutMs (1 s) bounds the block a turn builds automatically, because every turn pays it. context.advisor.timeoutMs (3 s) bounds a command a person is waiting on, and --timeout-ms overrides it for one call. A source that misses its deadline says so in the same answer instead of shortening it silently: on a large Transcript Lake archive the search takes seconds, so the automatic block usually reports timed out after 1000 ms for transcripts and jeden context recommend "…" --source transcripts --timeout-ms 20000 is how you actually read it.

An unknown source name is refused rather than dropped: unknown source(s): nonsense. Known sources: files, ground-truth, memory, transcripts. A narrowed answer is never the result of a typo.

Reading a short list#

Every answer carries a state for every source it consulted: available or unavailable, the observed reason, how much was considered, how much was returned, and how long it took. A list that is short because a source refused therefore looks different from a list that is short because nothing matched.

The files source also says when its own walk was cut: a root nobody sized cannot stall a turn, so the walk stops at its deadline or its cap and the detail then reads the walk stopped at its deadline or cap, so this is a partial corpus.

jeden context sources asks the same question with no query: which roots exist and how many chunks they hold, how many active memories the store carries, which runtime partitions the archive holds, and whether the ground-truth endpoint answers its health route. A configured endpoint nobody serves reports the URL it could not reach, not silence.

How a recommendation is ranked#

The files source weighs each query word by how rare it is in the corpus it just read, so a word that occurs in nearly every chunk contributes nearly nothing and no list of words to ignore exists anywhere in the product. A hit in a heading, a declaration or a path outweighs a hit in a body; covering more of the query outweighs repeating one word; a long chunk is damped so length alone cannot win.

A word also matches its own stem, so routingu finds routing and signing finds signed, at half the weight of an exact hit. Matching is lexical: a question asked in one language does not reach a document written in another unless they share words, and product names usually are those shared words.

The other three sources rank with their own engines — the memory store's index, Transcript Lake's query, the ground-truth index's score — because each owns its own corpus. Scores are therefore comparable inside a source and not across sources, so the answer interleaves them in a fixed order instead of sorting one list by number.

The same advisor in an Omp session#

Omp is not Jeden's to patch, and it does not need to be: it loads custom tools from ~/.omp/agent/tools/*.ts. jeden context install --omp renders a context_recommend tool into that directory, bound to the absolute path of the Jeden binary that rendered it, and that tool calls jeden context recommend --json. One implementation, two harnesses.

jeden context installed --omp reports current, stale or absent and exits non-zero unless the installed file is exactly what this binary renders, so an upgrade that changes the tool is visible instead of silent. --file &lt;path&gt; writes or checks any other location, which is how the product's own tests drive it.

Every surface#

CLI: jeden context recommend, prompt, sources, install, installed. A bare first word is the task, so jeden context "why does signing fail" works.

Interactive: /context &lt;task&gt; renders the same recommendations; bare /context keeps reporting the live window size.

Agent tool: context_recommend takes query, and optionally limit, sources and timeoutMs. It is a read-tier tool, because it does what the prologue already does unapproved.

RPC and Jeden Desktop: context/recommend and context/sources answer the same objects the CLI prints with --json. Desktop's Context screen is that RPC, not a parsed command line.

Configuration#

Every key below is in jeden config list and can be set per user in ~/.jeden/config.yml or per project in &lt;cwd&gt;/.jeden/config.json.

context.advisor.enabled (default true) appends the block to every task prompt. context.advisor.limit (default 6) is how many recommendations one answer carries. context.advisor.maxChars (default 6000) is the injected block's budget. context.advisor.timeoutMs (default 3000) and context.advisor.promptTimeoutMs (default 1000) are the per-source deadlines for a command and for the automatic block.

context.advisor.sources (default all) selects the sources every run consults. context.advisor.roots (default empty, meaning the project and ~/.jeden) declares the roots the files source walks. context.advisor.fileExtensions (default empty, meaning every readable text file) narrows it to named extensions. context.advisor.groundTruthUrl and context.advisor.transcriptLakeBin point the two external sources somewhere other than their defaults.
